steward.role: Nation Steward of Central African Republic

hero.lead: A nation of 5.5 million with forest over seven tenths of its land and nearly all its power from water, rebuilding its public finances with the IMF.

capital.heading: Forest and water, waiting for capital.

record.text: IMF Extended Credit Facility, approved April 2023; $58 million disbursed in June 2025
Public sector debt, share of GDP, projected for 2025, from 60.7% in 2024
Public debt including arrears, end March 2026, 59.89% of GDP; arrears of about FCFA 165 billion
Expenditure in the 2026 Finance Law, adopted 10 December 2025, against revenue of FCFA 368.43 billion; a financing need of FCFA 172.66 billion

register.name: Humanitarian Response Plan 2026
register.detail: Launched in Bangui, 5 February 2026 · 1.3 million people targeted
register.note: 2.3 million people in need, 35 per cent of the population
register.text: The appeal of the humanitarian community for 2026, for the 1.3 million most vulnerable Central Africans. In 2025, US$116.9 million was mobilised, only 36 per cent of what was required, and 116 humanitarian bases closed. Humanitarian aid remains a lifeline for 2.3 million people; if funding falls short, the plan puts the most acute needs first.

register.name: Douala–Bangui Economic Corridor, Phase 1
register.detail: Approved 12 June 2026 · IDA · first phase of a $1.12 billion multiphase programme with Cameroon and CEMAC
register.note: The Central African Republic’s share of a $525 million first phase
register.text: The first phase of a programme to modernise the corridor of more than 1,400 kilometres between Douala and Bangui, where transport costs run as high as $270 a ton and a journey takes 9 to 12 days. It rehabilitates priority road sections to climate-resilient standards and develops logistics hubs and feeder roads. For a landlocked nation, the cost of this road bears on the price of food and on every livelihood.

register.name: Extended Credit Facility
register.detail: IMF · Approved April 2023 · Extension requested April 2026
register.text: Third and fourth reviews completed 4 June 2025, with $58 million disbursed.

register.name: Budget support loan from France
register.detail: AFD release of 22 October 2025 · €15 million on signing of the agreement · €10 million at the end of 2025, subject to approval of the IMF’s fifth programme review
register.text: A loan from France through the AFD, paid in two tranches, after a €10 million budget support grant in 2024. It supports macroeconomic stability, essential health spending such as vaccines, targeted free care and medicines, and the clearing of domestic debt and wage arrears. Its health spending serves the health standard directly.

register.name: Emergency rehabilitation of the Boali hydroelectric plant
register.detail: AFD release of 2 July 2025 · grant
register.note: Nearly €5.2 million, as the AFD states
register.text: A grant from the AFD for the emergency rehabilitation of the hydroelectric plant at Boali. Almost all the nation’s power comes from water, so keeping its hydroelectric plants running serves the energy standard.

register.name: Trade finance guarantee for Ecobank Centrafrique
register.detail: Signed in Bangui, 29 April 2026 · trade finance transaction guarantee facility
register.note: The first collaboration between Ecobank Centrafrique and the African Development Bank Group
register.text: An African Development Bank guarantee that lets Ecobank Centrafrique finance imports of industrial inputs, agricultural production machinery and telecommunications equipment, with a focus on agro-industry and light manufacturing. It widens trade credit in the country, for the livelihood and food standards.

register.name: Climate-resilient water, sanitation and hygiene for vulnerable children (FP303)
register.detail: Approved 2 July 2026 · grant · total value $73.8 million, with $4.7 million of in-kind co-financing · UNICEF with the Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development
register.note: About 504,600 people directly and 2.56 million indirectly
register.text: A Green Climate Fund grant to make water, sanitation and hygiene services in climate-exposed areas more resilient to floods and droughts, and to strengthen disaster risk management. Only 6.2% of Central Africans have safely managed drinking water: this grant serves the water and shelter standards first.

register.name: Payments for environmental services in and around Bangui
register.detail: Approved 22 June 2026 · 60 months · $8.09 million through UNDP, $1.91 million paid by the CAFI Fund directly to beneficiaries
register.text: A project of the Central African Forest Initiative, carried out by UNDP, that pays for environmental services in Bangui and its surroundings. Part of the money goes from the CAFI Fund directly to beneficiaries after the results, so that care of the land around the capital earns an income, for the livelihood standard.

register.name: Bangui-M’Poko airport project
register.detail: Named in the AfDB release of 30 September 2026 · African Development Fund grant
register.note: Approval date not stated in the release
register.text: A grant from the African Development Fund for the Bangui-M’Poko international airport, the country’s main air link. It serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: EU humanitarian aid, 2026
register.detail: Announced 22 April 2026 · Part of €235 million for West and Central Africa · Multi-sector aid
register.note: EU humanitarian funding for the Central African Republic in 2026
register.text: Humanitarian funding from the European Union for a country where 2.3 million people need assistance. It serves the food, water, shelter and health standards.

register.name: Sakaï solar plant, 50 MW with 15 MWh battery
register.detail: Inaugurated August 2026 · Built by Global South Utilities in ten months from August 2025 · Feeds ENERCA, the national utility
register.note: A commitment of $90 million to a 65 MW Sakaï 2 is reported in the press; not confirmed for this plant
register.text: A solar plant near Bangui, built and owned by the Abu Dhabi-based Global South Utilities, expected to raise national generating capacity by more than 60%. It serves the energy standard.

register.name: IFAD programme, Debt Sustainability Framework grant
register.detail: Executive Board, December 2025 · Document EB 2025/146/R.7/Rev.1 · Total programme cost $63.041 million
register.text: A grant from the International Fund for Agricultural Development, on Debt Sustainability Framework terms, for a rural development programme. It serves the food and livelihood standards.

register.name: Humanitarian Response Plan 2025
register.detail: Launched in Bangui, 7 March 2025 · 1.8 million people targeted · Less than 40% funded
register.text: The 2025 plan of the Government and the Humanitarian Country Team, later reprioritised. It served the food, water, shelter, health and education standards.

register.name: Corridor 13, Gouga–Mbaïki–Bangui road, phase 1
register.detail: Works launched 18 April 2025 · African Development Fund and Transition Support Facility grant · 221 km · Mongoumba river port begun 10 December 2025
register.note: First phase of the Pointe-Noire–Bangui corridor
register.text: A grant from the African Development Bank Group’s concessional windows for the first phase of Corridor 13, a second route from Bangui to the port of Pointe-Noire. It serves the food and livelihood standards by cutting the cost of goods.

register.name: Public securities on the BEAC market, 2026 programme
register.detail: Finance Law 2026 · Financing need of FCFA 172.66 billion, mostly through public securities · Stock of securities FCFA 462.34 billion at end July 2026
register.note: The financing need the Treasury plans to cover, mostly on the regional market
register.text: Treasury bills and bonds sold on the regional market of the Bank of Central African States to fund the budget. Buybacks in 2026 drew little interest, a sign of a tight market.
by: Treasury of the Central African Republic

register.name: Inclusive and Resilient Cities (PROVIR), GEF additional grant
register.detail: Release of 22 July 2025 · Global Environment Facility grant, managed by the World Bank · Nature-based solutions
register.text: An additional grant for nature-based solutions to flooding in the cities covered by PROVIR. It serves the shelter and water standards.

register.name: Oubangui basin water resources and infrastructure, with the DR Congo
register.detail: Approved 20 September 2024 · Abidjan · African Development Fund · $118.27 million grant to the Central African Republic and $16.44 million loan to the DR Congo
register.note: The Central African Republic’s grant within $134.71 million
register.text: A grant for water resources and infrastructure in Greater Bangui, part of a programme on both banks of the Oubangui that is to benefit more than 2.4 million people. It serves the water standard.

register.name: Inclusive and Resilient Cities Project (PROVIR)
register.detail: Approved 10 September 2024 · IDA grant · Bangui and Berberati
register.text: An IDA grant for basic infrastructure and services and climate resilience in Bangui and Berberati, with a focus on displaced people, women and young people. It serves the shelter, water and livelihood standards.

register.name: Adaptive and Productive Social Safety Net
register.detail: Approved May 2024 · IDA grant
register.note: Social safety nets for vulnerable households
register.text: An IDA grant to expand social safety nets for vulnerable households. It serves the food and livelihood standards.

register.name: Maïngo, women and girls’ empowerment, additional financing
register.detail: Approved 10 April 2024 · IDA · Project P181574 · Original project of $50 million approved 23 June 2021
register.text: Additional IDA financing for health services, education and jobs for women and adolescent girls, including scholarships for girls to the end of secondary school. It serves the education, health and livelihood standards.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: One of Africa’s great forests: carbon, timber and biodiversity that can earn while they stand.
items.alt: Dense rainforest along the Sangha River in the south-west of the Central African Republic

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: Almost all the power that flows comes from water; the task is to bring it to the four in five still without it.
items.alt: A small hydroelectric plant below waterfalls with power lines, Central African Republic

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: Rain and rivers renewed every year: power, irrigation and drinking water.
items.alt: The wide Ubangi River at dawn with forested banks, Central African Republic

items.name: The Ground
items.label: Of GDP from natural resource rents, 2021
items.text: What lies under the land already earns; the task is to turn the rent into lasting assets.
items.alt: Red laterite rock and mineral-bearing gravel along a savanna river, Central African Republic

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 48.7% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.
items.alt: A tree-lined avenue and market in Bangui with people in the distance, Central African Republic

enterprises.heading: Already working in Central African Republic.

items.name: Global South Utilities
items.text: An Abu Dhabi-based company that opened a 50-megawatt solar complex with a 15 MWh battery at Sakai, near Bangui, in August 2026. The plant is expected to raise national generating capacity by more than 60 per cent.

items.name: Ecobank Centrafrique
items.text: A commercial bank in Bangui. Under a €5 million African Development Bank guarantee signed in April 2026, it finances imports of industrial inputs, agricultural production machinery and telecommunications equipment, with a focus on agro-industry and light manufacturing.

items.name: Établissement Mbêwih
items.text: A small firm founded in 2020 in Bangui’s seventh arrondissement that processes maize and sweet potato into flour, and has begun small-scale production.
